subject: Activation triggers, fallback policy and data synchronization for multi-region DR
messages:

Subject: Questions on activation triggers and data sync for multi-region DR

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the RFP materials so far. The DR section of our procurement team has a few follow-ups we need clarified for scoring:

- Exact activation triggers (what events cause automatic regional failover vs. manual switchover)
- Expected RTO and RPO targets at the service layer and for customer persistent data
- How in-flight sessions/requests are handled and whether we maintain session affinity
- Consistency and durability guarantees for the KV/prefix cache and any warm-up expectations after failover
- What evidence you can provide post-test (logs, traces, smoke-test results)

Can you send a short mapping of events -> action (auto/manual), an example rollback path, and a small runbook excerpt and architecture diagram? Our deadline for the RFP addendum is 2026-11-26.

Appreciate it,
Aisha

Cobalt Financial

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on activation triggers and data sync for multi-region DR

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. I’ve attached a short DR overview and a sanitized runbook excerpt that addresses the items you called out (see attachments). High level answers below; I’ll follow up with a one-page event->action matrix and a proposed evidence bundle.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Activation triggers:
  - Automatic: total regional control-plane loss (health checks fail across primary cluster for 60s), cloud provider region outage signals, or sustained degradation beyond defined SLO thresholds (error rate > 10% for 5 consecutive minutes).
  - Manual: planned maintenance, partial hardware failures affecting a subset of shards, or customer-initiated rollback requests.
- RTO / RPO (service-layer defaults we propose for the contract):
  - Control-plane failover routing: target RTO 2 minutes (DNS/route update + routing policy).
  - Model-serving switchover (warm-up + KV recovery): target RTO 5 minutes for core inference paths; full cache warming up to baseline within 30 minutes depending on traffic rehits.
  - Persistent customer data: RPO depends on your replication settings. If you use our cross-region replication for customer storage, typical RPO is <60s; if you rely on single-region storage, RPO is best-effort.
- In-flight requests / session affinity:
  - We continue to attempt graceful draining on the failing region for up to 60s; requests that exceed timeout will be retried by the client. We recommend short client-side timeouts for failover-sensitive calls. Sticky sessions are not guaranteed across region switch unless implemented at the application layer (we can share patterns).
- KV / prefix cache consistency:
  - KV cache is an in-memory performance optimization; it is not a source of truth. We treat it as eventual — warm-up is expected after failover. Customers requiring strict consistency should use durable storage with cross-region replication.

Attachments included: redwood-drc-overview.pdf (summary), redwood-runbook-excerpt.txt (sanitized procedural steps), cross-region-architecture.png (high-level).

Proposed next step: I can send an event->action matrix and a short rollback criteria page by EOD tomorrow, and we can schedule a 30-minute failover demo + evidence review the week of Nov 29. Does Nov 30 at 10:00 AM ET work for your team?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions on activation triggers and data sync for multi-region DR

Naomi —

Thanks, that helps. A few clarifications before we commit the scoring:

1) Automatic vs manual triggers: can you share the exact health-check endpoints and the observability signals you monitor (e.g., 5xx rate, queue depth, provider region event)? We need to map these back to our incident response playbooks.

2) DNS / routing details: do you rely on DNS TTL changes for traffic shift, or do you use a global load-balancer with traffic steering? What's the effective cutover profile (churn from DNS TTL vs routing layer)?

3) Session behavior: you note a 60s drain window — what happens to requests that were accepted but not yet completed? Are they retried automatically?

4) Evidence package: we require (a) a representative smoke-test result from a failover rehearsal, (b) the runbook excerpt (sanitized is fine), and (c) service-side traces that show the switchover timeline. Can you confirm these will be included?

5) SLA credits: for a region-level outage that causes customer-impacting downtime > 30 minutes, what credit framework would you accept in the contract?

If you can provide a short (bulleted) answers doc plus the smoke-test artifact, we can clear this section.

Regards,
Aisha

[Sent on behalf of Cobalt Financial - DR Review]

Subject: Fwd: Questions on activation triggers and data sync for multi-region DR — internal answer draft

Ben / Karthik —

Please see Aisha's follow-ups below. Draft answers and action items:

Draft answers to send to Cobalt (short bullets):
- Health checks / observability signals: we monitor control-plane heartbeat, API 5xx rate (5m sliding window), queue/backpressure depth on inference workers, and cloud provider region incident events. Automatic failover is triggered when the control-plane heartbeat fails for 60s AND at least two additional health signals breach configured thresholds.
- Routing strategy: primary method is global traffic steering via GSLB/anycast with programmatic MAP updates — not DNS TTL changes alone. We set a conservative DNS TTL of 30s for customers who need it, but cutover is via routing plane update with expected client impact window of ~0-120s depending on client retries.
- In-flight requests: we attempt graceful drain for 60s. Requests accepted but not completed are not recovered by the old region; clients should retry idempotent requests. We'll include recommended client patterns in the sent doc.
- Evidence package: we can supply a sanitized smoke-test log (trace IDs and timeline), the runbook excerpt, and smoke-test graphs (latency and error rate pre/post).
- SLA credits: propose a negotiable credit table; for >30 minutes region outage we recommend 10% of monthly service fees for the impacted service window as a starting point (sales/legal to negotiate).

Action items:
- Ben: prepare sanitized smoke-test artifact (timeline, trace ids, graphs) and a one-page evidence bundle by EOD 11/20.
- Karthik: prepare security/compliance commentary on data residency and cross-region replication options and confirm any encryption/KMS notes for the evidence bundle.
- Naomi: finalize the short bullets and send to Aisha once Ben/Karthik confirm artifacts.

Let’s keep this concise and template-ready for other customers.

Thanks,
Naomi

Subject: Re: Questions on activation triggers and data sync for multi-region DR

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the follow-ups. Attaching the evidence bundle and a short event->action matrix. Answers in bullets below (condensed for the RFP):

- Health-checks / signals (what we monitor): control-plane heartbeat, API 5xx rate (5m window), inference worker queue depth, cloud provider outage signal. Auto-failover requires control-plane heartbeat failure for >=60s + one additional breached signal. Manual failover remains available to operators.

- Routing / cutover mechanism: primary: global steering (GSLB/anycast) with programmatic routing updates; we do not rely on DNS TTL changes as the only mechanism. Typical routing plane cutover effect is immediate but client-visible impact can range 0–120s depending on client retry behavior. We recommend a DNS TTL of 30s when customers want predictable TTL behavior.

- In-flight requests / sessions: graceful drain window of up to 60s. Requests accepted by the failing region and not completed are not replayed across regions by the platform; clients should retry idempotent requests. We include recommended client retry/backoff patterns in the evidence bundle.

- KV / cache: ephemeral performance cache only; not a source of truth. Warm-up depends on traffic profile — expect baseline warm-up within 30 minutes; critical state should be in durable storage with cross-region replication for strict RPO needs.

- Evidence package included: sanitized smoke-test timeline (trace ids and timestamps), runbook excerpt, architecture diagram, and pre/post error/latency graphs.

- SLA credits: our starting position for contract negotiation is a credit of 10% of monthly service fees for region-level outages exceeding 30 minutes, subject to terms. We can include a more detailed schedule in the SOW.

Next steps:
- We’ve scheduled a technical failover demo + evidence review for Nov 30, 10:00 AM ET. Please confirm attendees and any specific scenarios you want us to exercise (e.g., concurrent model load + storage failover).

If that meets your needs I’ll mark the RFP section as complete and upload the evidence to the shared drive link below.

Best regards,
Naomi Feldman
